description_full: Mobility Global, Inc. provides automotive data, insights, and technology solutions in the United States and internationally. It operates in two segments, CARFAX and Business-to-Business (B2B). The CARFAX segment provides consumers, dealers, car service providers, and finance and insurance with vehicle history, valuations, listings, and service reminders through proprietary data estate and brand to help consumers buy the right car at the right price, sell, and maintain vehicles. The B2B segment delivers data, forecasts, and sales and marketing solutions for product planning, supply-chain and technology decisions, market analytics, pricing and incentives, and targeted customer activation to original equipment manufacturers, suppliers, dealers, and finance and insurance markets. This segment also provides suite of solutions, including automotiveMastermind, Polk Auto Solutions, Market Scan, various market reporting tools, and Data Studio platform, as well as vehicle and supply chain forecasting, and global reporting. It sells its products through subscription and non-subscription transactions. The company was formerly known as S&P Global Mobility Holding Company and changed its name to Mobility Global, Inc. in February 2026. The company was incorporated in 2025 and is based in Centreville, Virginia.

financial_summary: Mobility Global Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.3B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $461M in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.46× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.3× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
